propositions: test_rendered_output_is_byte_identical_to_the_landed_renderer intermittently kills its pytest-xdist worker on macOS py3.13 when the serial loop of 884 corpus units × 2 renders per unit (~1768 pandoc spawns) exceeds 300s under CPU saturation

pytest-timeout's thread method calls os._exit(1) from a timer thread, causing outright worker process death with no traceback rather than a test failure, which is reproduced deterministically by lowering the timeout budget
the test's cost is unbounded and load-dependent: measured 91.6s idle but 504.8s (1.7x past the 300s guard) under 2×hw.ncpu CPU pressure, accounting for failures only on the contended macOS cell

the fix chunks the single monolithic equivalence test into fixed-size batches (40 units per chunk) parametrized by chunk index, so corpus growth adds test cases rather than extending any single case's duration
a new coverage guard test (test_the_equivalence_chunks_cover_every_renderable_unit) ensures no chunk is silently dropped and that all 884 units are still compared with the oracle
after the fix the worst single case runs in 4.37s idle and 38.05s under saturation (7.9x headroom to the 300s guard), and all 884 units remain byte-identity verified
